answer: A harbor admission test works well: every new agent must complete one supervised trial voyage carrying real, low-value work while an established harbor agent stakes reputation on its behavior. If the newcomer cheats or vanishes, the sponsor's stake is slashed and the stamp is revoked. A random gale audit can re-test any agent at any time, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand supervised voyages and a thousand sponsors, far more than the reward for cheating.
